devices.name: Synecdoche
devices.definition: Substituting a part for the whole, or the whole for a part (“all the world”; “flesh and blood”).

occurrences.note: " O Thou that hearest prayer, unto Thee shall all flesh come ": i.e., all people
" My flesh also shall rest in hope ": i.e., my body will rest in hope
" Thou wilt not leave my soul (i.e., me) in Hades": i.e., the grave
" I humbled my soul (i.e., myself) with fasting."
" Man being in honour, abideth not: he is like the beasts that perish."
"They gather themselves together against the soul of the righteous (i.e., against the righteous man), and condemn the innocent blood ": i.e., the innocent man
"As for man, his days are as grass": i.e., he himself, or his life
"We have sinned with our fathers ": i.e., with all who have gone before
" All nations compassed me about ": i.e., a great many
" For thy servant David's sake turn not away the face of thine anointed." Here the figure emphasizes the last words, meaning not his face merely, but David himself

devices.name: Idiom
devices.definition: A peculiar usage of the Hebrew or Greek that does not carry its literal force — an idiom to be rendered by its sense, not word for word.

occurrences.note: sometimes even italics are omitted, and the passage is most obscure

" Forget not all his benefits": i.e., forget not any

devices.name: Heterosis
devices.definition: Exchange of one grammatical form for another — of tense, number, person, degree, or mood (e.g. a future used for a command).

occurrences.note: " Thou hast anointed ": i.e., wilt anoint
" My God, in thee I have trusted: " i.e., do I trust

" Send thine hands from above; rid me and deliver me ": i.e., send thy gracious protection and great delivering power. The singular is actually the Textual reading, not only in some Manuscripts

devices.name: Gnome (quotation)
devices.definition: A quotation or proverbial maxim woven in — a pithy saying cited for authority or point.

devices.definition: A question asked for effect, not for an answer — to affirm, deny, or provoke thought.

devices.definition: Giving human traits, action, or speech to something impersonal or abstract.

devices.name: Pleonasm
devices.definition: A deliberate redundancy — more words than strictly needed — to underline or solemnise.

devices.name: Paronomasia (wordplay)
devices.definition: A play on words that sound alike but differ in sense — pun, rhyme, near-repetition.

devices.name: Simile
devices.definition: An explicit comparison of two unlike things using “like” or “as.”

occurrences.note: " He shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water." Here, the similitude tells us that the man who meditates in God's word is planted and protected, just as a tree in a garden is cared for

devices.name: Anaphora
devices.definition: The same word or phrase begins a run of successive clauses, hammering a theme.

occurrences.note: (twice), 5, 7, 8, 9. — Where seven times we have the words, " The voice of the Lord," commencing seven successive clauses. The number of spiritual perfection

devices.name: Polysyndeton
devices.definition: Conjunctions (“and … and …”) piled up to slow the pace and weight every item.

devices.name: Enigma
devices.definition: A dark saying — a truth wrapped in obscure or riddling terms.

devices.name: Epanadiplosis
devices.definition: A clause encircled — beginning and ending with the same word.

occurrences.note: (5, 11). — Where we have the sentence repeated, to emphasize the fact that when our enemies seem mightiest, we can say, " In God will I praise His word."
" God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, that did seek God."

devices.name: Anadiplosis
devices.definition: The word ending one clause is repeated to begin the next, linking them.

" The Lord hath been mindful of us, and He will bless: He will bless the house of Israel. He will bless the house of Aaron. He will bless them that fear the Lord,"

devices.name: Hypotyposis
devices.definition: Vivid word-painting that sets a scene before the eyes as though present.

that of the righteous to the palm and the cedar

devices.name: Synonymia
devices.definition: Amassing synonyms — words of like meaning — to enforce and enlarge a point.

devices.name: Epizeuxis
devices.definition: Immediate repetition of a word for intense emphasis, with nothing between (“Lord, Lord”).

occurrences.note: (7, 8).- " God shall bless us, God shall bless us: " i.e., God shall really and truly bless us in very deed
" Sing praises to God, sing praises: Sing praises unto our King, sing praises."
" For He cometh, for He cometh: " i.e., for He shall surely come

devices.name: Paroemia (proverb)
devices.definition: A proverb — a wayside-saying in common use, cited or coined.

devices.name: Polyptoton
devices.definition: Repetition of the same root word in different inflections (“dying you shall die”).

occurrences.note: Here the noun is actually supplied in the A.V. " Sleep the sleep of death," i.e, sleep the last solemn sleep of death
" Cast forth lightning." Heb., lighten lightning, i.e., lighten exceedingly, and destroy them

devices.name: Hyperbole
devices.definition: Deliberate exaggeration, not meant literally, that drives a point home vividly.

devices.name: Parallelism
devices.definition: Successive lines echo one another in structure — saying the same thing twice, or balancing matched clauses.

devices.name: Periphrasis
devices.definition: Circumlocution: a description put in place of the plain name of a thing.

occurrences.note: " Thou hast put gladness in my heart, more than in the time that their corn and their wine increased ": i.e., more than in the joy of their abundant harvest and vintage

devices.name: Symploce
devices.definition: Anaphora and epistrophe together — clauses that share both their opening and closing words.

devices.name: Anabasis
devices.definition: A gradual ascent — a series that mounts, clause by clause, to a high point.

occurrences.note: " Let the enemy persecute my soul, and take it; Yea, let him tread down my life upon the earth. And lay mine honour in the dust."

devices.name: Catachresis
devices.definition: One word used for another only remotely related — a deliberately incongruous transfer.

devices.name: Hendiadys
devices.definition: One idea expressed by two words joined with “and,” the second really qualifying the first.

occurrences.note: "Give unto the Loud glory and strength": i.e., glory, yes — and great glory too

devices.name: Polyonymia
devices.definition: Heaping up several different names or titles for the same person or thing.

devices.name: Acrostic
devices.definition: Successive lines or stanzas begin with the letters of the alphabet in order — a Hebrew form that cannot survive translation (Pss 25, 34, 119; Lam 1–4; Prov 31:10–31).

devices.name: Antonomasia
devices.definition: A proper name replaced by a descriptive title, or a title by a proper name (“the Son of man”).

devices.name: Epiphonema
devices.definition: A closing exclamation that sums up and drives home what has just been said.

occurrences.note: " Blessed are all they that put their trust in him."
" Salvation belongeth unto the Lord. Thy blessing is upon Thy people."
At the conclusion of the Psalm, this exclamation is added: " Oh, that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion ! " etc

devices.name: Irony
devices.definition: Saying the opposite of what is meant, so the real sense is felt through the contrast.

devices.name: Dialogismus
devices.definition: The speaker dramatises a dialogue, putting words into another's mouth.

devices.name: Ecphonesis
devices.definition: An outcry of feeling — a sudden exclamation breaking from strong emotion (“O the depth!”).

occurrences.note: also a beautiful Ecphonesis

devices.name: Euphemism
devices.definition: A softened or decent expression put for one that is harsh or delicate (“fallen asleep”).

occurrences.note: with special reference to the reception of the.Messiah: and all who were truly wise submitted themselves. Those who did not are thus rebuked
" Unless the Lord had been my help, my soul had almost (marg., quickly) dwelt in silence": i.e., I should soon have been dead and buried

devices.name: Hermeneia
devices.definition: Interpretation: a plain restatement added at once to explain a figure just used.

devices.name: Hypallage
devices.definition: Interchange: a word logically belonging to one term is grammatically attached to another.

devices.name: Metaphor
devices.definition: An implied comparison that calls one thing another (“A is B”), without “like” or “as.”

occurrences.note: have the same fact stated literally as a Simile. See page
" His truth is a shield and a buckler" (R.V.). Here, we have the Metaphor, by which the one thing is carried over and stated as being the other

devices.name: Palinodia
devices.definition: A concession — granting a point for argument's sake before answering it.

devices.name: Tapeinosis
devices.definition: Deliberate understatement — belittling a thing to magnify it, or lessening to increase the effect.

occurrences.note: "A broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise: " i.e.. Thou wilt graciously accept and welcome and bless
" And suffereth not their cattle to decrease: " i.e., will abundantly multiply their cattle

devices.name: Allegory
devices.definition: An extended metaphor — a whole passage whose surface story stands throughout for a deeper meaning.

devices.name: Antimetabole
devices.definition: Words repeated in reverse order and grammatical relation (“sabbath for man … man for sabbath”).

devices.name: Antiptosis
devices.definition: One grammatical case put for another (commonly a genitive doing the work of an adjective).

devices.name: Aposiopesis
devices.definition: A sentence broken off unfinished, as if the speaker cannot or will not go on.

devices.name: Climax
devices.definition: A chain in which the end of each step becomes the start of the next, building to a peak.

devices.name: Epitheton
devices.definition: Naming a thing by an attribute or adjunct added to it (“John the Baptist”).

devices.name: Hyperbaton
devices.definition: Words wrenched out of their natural order, throwing weight onto the displaced word.

devices.name: Hysteresis
devices.definition: A later passage supplying a detail not recorded in the earlier narrative it refers to.

occurrences.note: " Whose feet they hurt with fetters." This, by Hysteresis, is mentioned here, though not recorded in the history of Joseph in Genesis

devices.name: Maledictio
devices.definition: An imprecation or pronouncement of woe (“Woe to you…”).

devices.name: Parable
devices.definition: A continued simile — a narrative laid alongside a truth to teach it by comparison.

devices.name: Zeugma
devices.definition: One verb made to govern two objects though it strictly fits only one; the second borrows it.
